Formula: Cauchy-Riemann Differential Equations
Exact Expression: \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} = -\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}
Definitions: System of two partial differential equations forming the necessary and sufficient condition for a complex function to be complex differentiable (holomorphic).
Derivation/Reference: Jean le Rond d'Alembert (1752); Augustin-Louis Cauchy (1814); Bernhard Riemann (1851 doctoral dissertation)
Example: f(z) = z^2 = (x+iy)^2 = (x^2 - y^2) + i(2xy) -> u=x^2-y^2, v=2xy -> u_x = 2x = v_y; u_y = -2y = -v_x. Holomorphic everywhere.
Domain: complex_analysis
Assumptions: u and v have continuous first partial derivatives in neighborhood of z_0
Common Errors: Assuming real differentiability of u and v implies complex differentiability without verifying CR equations
subject: Cauchy-Riemann Differential Equations
